title: Design a parking lot
brief: Design the object model for a multi-level parking garage. Vehicles of different sizes arrive, get assigned a compatible spot, receive a ticket, and pay on exit based on time parked. Focus on classes and how they collaborate, not on hardware.
constraints: Multiple floors, each with motorcycle, compact, large and EV-charging spots
Vehicle types: motorcycle, car, truck; a smaller vehicle may use a larger spot
Hourly pricing that may vary by spot type
Several entry and exit gates operating concurrently
No reservations in the first version

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
sections.prompt: Pin down the actors, the main use cases and what is explicitly out of scope.
keyPoints: Use cases: park (assign spot, issue ticket), unpark (compute fee, pay, free spot), show availability per floor/type
Actors: driver, entry/exit gate, attendant/admin who configures floors and rates
Fit rules: motorcycle -> any spot, car -> compact or large, truck -> large only
Full lot must reject at the entry gate with a clear message
Non-goals: reservations, license plate recognition, payment processor internals

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
sections.prompt: List the core classes and the single responsibility of each.
keyPoints: ParkingLot: aggregate root holding floors, gates and the spot-assignment strategy
Level/Floor: owns its ParkingSpots and per-type free counts
ParkingSpot (id, type, occupant) with canFit(Vehicle) and assign/release
Vehicle (abstract) with Motorcycle, Car, Truck subclasses exposing size
Ticket (id, vehicle, spot, entryTime, exitTime, status) and Payment
EntryGate/ExitGate as thin controllers delegating to ParkingLot

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
sections.prompt: Describe composition vs association and the interfaces that decouple policy from structure.
keyPoints: ParkingLot composes Levels; Level composes ParkingSpots (lifetime owned)
Ticket associates a Vehicle with a ParkingSpot; spot holds a back-reference only while occupied
SpotAssignmentStrategy interface: findSpot(Vehicle, levels) -> Optional<ParkingSpot>
PricingStrategy interface: calculate(Ticket, now) -> Money
PaymentProcessor interface so cash/card/app are interchangeable

sections.title: Key methods & flows
sections.prompt: Walk through park and unpark with method signatures.
keyPoints: Ticket ParkingLot.park(Vehicle v): strategy.findSpot -> spot.assign(v) -> new Ticket(v, spot, clock.now())
Money ExitGate.computeFee(Ticket t) -> pricing.calculate(t, clock.now())
Receipt ExitGate.pay(Ticket t, PaymentMethod m) marks ticket PAID
void ParkingLot.unpark(Ticket t): validate PAID, spot.release(), level.incrementFree(type)
Map<SpotType,Integer> getAvailability(levelId) served from counters, not scans

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
sections.prompt: Which patterns apply and how would you add new spot types or pricing rules?
keyPoints: Strategy for spot assignment (nearest-to-entrance, fill-lowest-floor) and pricing
Factory for creating Vehicle/Spot from type enums
Singleton-ish ParkingLot only if justified; prefer dependency injection
Observer to push availability changes to display boards
Open/closed: new EV spot = new SpotType + fit rule, no edits to park()

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
sections.prompt: Two cars at different gates want the last compact spot. What happens? Other edge cases?
keyPoints: Spot assignment must be atomic: lock per spot or compareAndSet on occupant
Per-level lock or concurrent free-spot queues to avoid a global bottleneck
Lost ticket: charge max daily rate, look up by plate
Payment succeeds but gate fails: ticket status PAID lets driver retry exit
Clock injection for testable fee calculation across midnight/daylight saving

modelSummary: The ParkingLot aggregate owns Levels, which own ParkingSpots typed by size. Vehicles are an abstract hierarchy with a size used by ParkingSpot.canFit. Entry gates call ParkingLot.park, which delegates to a SpotAssignmentStrategy and issues a Ticket. Exit gates compute the fee via a PricingStrategy and take payment via a PaymentProcessor before unpark releases the spot. Availability is kept in per-level counters and published to display boards via Observer. Spot claiming is atomic (CAS on occupant or per-level lock) so concurrent gates never double-assign. Classes: ParkingLot, Level, ParkingSpot, SpotType, Vehicle{Motorcycle,Car,Truck}, Ticket, Payment, EntryGate, ExitGate, SpotAssignmentStrategy, PricingStrategy, PaymentProcessor.

title: Design an elevator system
brief: Design the control software for a bank of elevators in an office building. Riders press up/down hall buttons and floor buttons inside the car. Your controller decides which car serves which request. Model the classes and the scheduling logic.
constraints: N elevators (e.g. 4) serving M floors (e.g. 30)
Hall calls (floor + direction) and car calls (destination inside the car)
Each car has capacity and a door; maintenance/emergency modes exist
Simulation-friendly: time advances in ticks
Optimise average wait time, not strict fairness

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
sections.prompt: Clarify request types, states and what "good" scheduling means.
keyPoints: Hall call = (floor, direction); car call = destination from inside a specific car
Car states: IDLE, MOVING_UP, MOVING_DOWN, DOORS_OPEN, MAINTENANCE
Must not reverse direction while it still has requests ahead (SCAN/LOOK)
Emergency stop and fire mode override normal scheduling
Non-goals: physical motor control, destination dispatch kiosks

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: ElevatorController/Dispatcher: receives hall calls and assigns them to cars
ElevatorCar: id, currentFloor, direction, state, up/down stop sets
Request (HallRequest, CarRequest) value objects
Door with open/close and obstruction sensor
Floor/HallPanel and CarPanel as input sources
SchedulingStrategy chooses which car takes a hall call

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
sections.prompt: How do the pieces talk to each other?
keyPoints: Controller has many ElevatorCars; each car owns its Door and stop queues
Panels depend on a RequestSink interface implemented by the controller (or car for car calls)
SchedulingStrategy interface: ElevatorCar select(HallRequest, List<ElevatorCar>)
Cars publish state changes (arrived, doorsOpened) to listeners: panels light up/clear
State pattern: ElevatorState implementations handle tick() and onRequest()

sections.title: Key methods & flows
sections.prompt: Walk a hall call from button press to the rider stepping out.
keyPoints: void HallPanel.press(Direction d) -> controller.submit(new HallRequest(floor, d))
ElevatorCar Controller.submit(HallRequest r): strategy.select(r, cars).addStop(r.floor, r.dir)
void ElevatorCar.tick(): if stop at currentFloor -> openDoors(); else move one floor in direction
Next stop: TreeSet upStops.ceiling(current) when going up; flip direction only when empty (LOOK)
void CarPanel.press(int floor) -> car.addStop(floor) directly

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
sections.prompt: Which patterns, and how do you swap the dispatch algorithm?
keyPoints: Strategy: nearest-car, LOOK-cost, zoning (low/high-rise banks)
State pattern for car modes; maintenance just refuses new assignments
Observer for lights and displays
Command objects for requests make logging and replay simple
Cost function: distance + penalty for opposite direction + load factor

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
sections.prompt: Discuss concurrent button presses and failure cases.
keyPoints: Controller processes requests on a single event loop or with a lock per car
Duplicate hall presses are idempotent (set semantics)
Car goes to maintenance: reassign its pending hall calls to other cars
Full car skips hall pickups but still serves car calls
Door obstruction keeps doors open with a timeout and alarm

modelSummary: A central ElevatorController receives HallRequests from floor panels and uses a pluggable SchedulingStrategy to assign each to an ElevatorCar via a cost function. Each car keeps up and down stop sets (sorted) and runs LOOK: serve stops in the current direction, reverse only when none remain. Car calls go directly to the car. ElevatorCar behaviour is modelled with the State pattern (Idle, MovingUp, MovingDown, DoorsOpen, Maintenance) and time advances via tick(). Observers update hall lanterns and displays. Requests are idempotent sets, and a car entering maintenance hands its pending hall calls back to the controller. Classes: ElevatorController, ElevatorCar, ElevatorState, Door, HallRequest, CarRequest, Direction, HallPanel, CarPanel, SchedulingStrategy.

title: Design an in-memory file system
brief: Design an in-memory file system that supports directories and files addressed by absolute paths like /a/b/c.txt. Support mkdir -p, ls, writing and appending to files, reading, and deleting. Think about the class hierarchy and path resolution.
constraints: Absolute Unix-style paths, "/" as root
Operations: mkdir, ls, createFile, append, read, rm (recursive optional), move
ls on a file returns just that file name; ls on a dir returns sorted children
Single process, but multiple threads may call it
No persistence or permissions in v1

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
sections.prompt: Define operations and their semantics on errors.
keyPoints: mkdir(path) creates intermediate directories (mkdir -p semantics)
ls returns lexicographically sorted names; on a file returns [name]
append to a missing file creates it; read of missing path throws NotFound
rm of non-empty dir requires recursive flag
Errors: PathNotFound, NotADirectory, AlreadyExists, IsADirectory

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: Entry (abstract): name, parent, createdAt, modifiedAt, size()
Directory extends Entry: Map<String,Entry> children (TreeMap for sorted ls)
File extends Entry: StringBuilder/byte[] content
FileSystem facade: root Directory and path operations
Path value object: parse("/a/b") -> ["a","b"], handles trailing slash and "."/".."

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
sections.prompt: Explain the hierarchy and why it is a Composite.
keyPoints: Composite pattern: Directory contains Entries, which may be Files or Directories
size() is recursive on Directory, direct on File
FileSystem depends on a PathResolver; entries do not know about string paths
Parent pointer enables getPath() and move without a full search
Optional Visitor for operations like find, du, serialize

sections.title: Key methods & flows
sections.prompt: Walk through mkdir, write and ls.
keyPoints: Directory resolve(Path p, boolean create): walk components from root, create missing dirs if create
void mkdir(String path) -> resolve(Path.parse(path), true)
void append(String path, String data): parent = resolve(p.parent(), true); file = parent.getOrCreateFile(name); file.append(data)
List<String> ls(String path): entry = lookup(path); entry is File ? [name] : sorted children keys
void move(String src, String dst): detach from old parent, rename, attach to new parent; reject moving a dir into its own subtree

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
sections.prompt: How would you extend it with permissions, links or search?
keyPoints: Composite for the tree; Visitor for find/du without bloating Entry
Permission checks via a decorator or an AccessPolicy interface on resolve
Symlinks as a new Entry subtype resolved with a hop limit to avoid cycles
Storage strategy interface so File content could be chunked or on disk
Observer for file watchers (onCreate, onModify)

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Coarse ReadWriteLock on the FileSystem is simplest and correct
Finer: per-directory locks acquired top-down in path order to avoid deadlock
move needs both parents locked in a consistent order (e.g. by path or id)
Edge cases: root "/" ls, trailing slashes, duplicate names across file/dir
Deleting a directory while another thread appends below it must fail cleanly

modelSummary: The file system is a Composite: abstract Entry with File and Directory subclasses, where Directory holds a TreeMap of children so ls is naturally sorted. A FileSystem facade parses paths into a Path value object and walks from root via resolve(path, create), which also implements mkdir -p. Files hold content in a buffer supporting append and read; size is recursive for directories. Parent pointers support getPath and move, which rejects moving a directory into its own subtree. Extensions use Visitor (find, du), decorators for permissions, and a Symlink entry with a hop limit. Concurrency starts with a ReadWriteLock and can be refined to ordered per-directory locks. Classes: FileSystem, Path, Entry, Directory, File, PathResolver, EntryVisitor.

title: Design a cache with pluggable eviction (LRU/LFU)
brief: Design a generic in-memory key-value cache with a fixed capacity. It should support get and put in O(1), and the eviction policy must be pluggable so we can choose LRU, LFU or others at construction time.
constraints: Generic Cache<K,V> with fixed max entries
get/put O(1) average for LRU and LFU
Optional per-entry TTL
Thread-safe for concurrent readers and writers
Expose hit/miss/eviction stats

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
sections.prompt: Define the API and behaviour at capacity.
keyPoints: get(k) returns value and counts as an access; put(k,v) inserts or updates
At capacity, put of a new key evicts exactly one victim chosen by policy
Update of an existing key never evicts
TTL-expired entries treated as misses and removed lazily
Eviction listener callback for metrics or write-back

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: Cache<K,V> interface and a default implementation holding Map<K,Entry<V>>
EvictionPolicy<K> interface: onAccess, onInsert, onRemove, evict() -> K
LRUPolicy: doubly linked list + node map; move-to-front on access
LFUPolicy: key->freq, freq->LinkedHashSet<K>, minFreq pointer
CacheStats and an optional Clock for TTL

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
sections.prompt: How does the cache talk to the policy?
keyPoints: Cache composes one EvictionPolicy injected via constructor (Strategy)
Cache owns storage; policy only tracks ordering metadata of keys
Policy never touches values: clean separation of concerns
EvictionListener<K,V> notified after removal
Builder: CacheBuilder.capacity(100).policy(new LFUPolicy()).ttl(...)

sections.title: Key methods & flows
sections.prompt: Walk through get and put under LRU and LFU.
keyPoints: V get(K k): e = map.get(k); if null or expired -> miss; policy.onAccess(k); return e.value
void put(K k, V v): if exists -> update, onAccess; else if size==cap -> victim = policy.evict(); map.remove(victim); then insert + onInsert
LRU evict(): remove tail of linked list in O(1)
LFU onAccess: move key from freq f bucket to f+1, bump minFreq if bucket f emptied and f==minFreq
LFU onInsert: freq=1, minFreq=1; evict(): pop oldest from bucket[minFreq] (LRU tiebreak)

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
sections.prompt: How do you add new policies or features without modifying the cache?
keyPoints: Strategy for eviction: FIFO, Random, ARC slot in by implementing EvictionPolicy
Decorator for stats, logging or synchronization around a base cache
Template method optional for common bookkeeping
Factory/Builder to configure capacity, TTL and policy
Write-through/write-back via a loader/writer interface (CacheLoader)

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
sections.prompt: Make it thread-safe and discuss pitfalls.
keyPoints: LRU mutates on every read, so a plain ReadWriteLock does not help get(); use a mutex
Lock striping/segmenting by key hash scales, each segment with its own policy (approximate global LRU)
Caffeine-style: record accesses in a buffer and apply to the policy asynchronously
Capacity 0, null keys/values, and put during eviction listener re-entrancy
Thundering herd on miss: computeIfAbsent with per-key futures

modelSummary: Cache<K,V> stores entries in a HashMap and delegates ordering decisions to an injected EvictionPolicy<K> (Strategy), which receives onInsert/onAccess/onRemove events and returns a victim from evict(). LRUPolicy uses a hashmap plus doubly linked list for O(1) move-to-front and tail eviction. LFUPolicy keeps key->frequency, frequency->LinkedHashSet buckets and a minFreq pointer, giving O(1) updates with LRU tiebreaking. Updates never evict; inserts at capacity evict exactly one key. TTL is checked lazily using an injected Clock. Thread safety starts with a single lock (reads mutate policy state) and scales via segmentation or buffered access recording. Classes: Cache, ConcurrentCache, EvictionPolicy, LRUPolicy, LFUPolicy, Entry, CacheStats, EvictionListener, CacheBuilder.

title: Design a library management system
brief: Design the object model for a public library. Members search the catalog, borrow and return physical copies, place holds on books that are checked out, and pay fines for late returns.
constraints: A title (Book) can have many physical copies (BookItem)
Members may borrow up to 5 items for 14 days
Holds queue in FIFO order per book
Late fee per day, capped
Librarians manage catalog and members

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
sections.prompt: List the use cases and business rules.
keyPoints: Search by title, author, subject, ISBN
Checkout, return, renew (blocked if holds exist), place/cancel hold
Fine accrues on overdue return; members with unpaid fines over threshold cannot borrow
Notifications on hold availability and due dates
Non-goals: e-books, inter-library loans

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: Book (ISBN, title, authors) vs BookItem (barcode, status, location)
Member and Librarian extending Account/Person
Loan (item, member, issuedAt, dueAt, returnedAt)
Hold (book, member, createdAt, status)
Fine; Catalog for search indexes; LibraryService facade

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
keyPoints: Book 1..* BookItem; Member 0..5 active Loans
Hold attaches to Book (any copy), Loan to a specific BookItem
Catalog exposes search interfaces by attribute (Map indexes)
FinePolicy interface computes amount from Loan
NotificationService interface (email/SMS)

sections.title: Key methods & flows
keyPoints: Loan checkout(memberId, barcode): validate member limits/fines, item AVAILABLE or RESERVED for this member, create Loan, item.status=LOANED
void returnItem(barcode): close Loan, fine = finePolicy.compute(loan, today)
On return: if holds queue non-empty -> item.status=RESERVED, notify head member, set pickup deadline
Loan renew(loanId): reject if holds exist or renew count exceeded
List<Book> Catalog.search(Query q)

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
keyPoints: Strategy for FinePolicy (per member type)
Observer for notifications on hold availability
State for BookItem (Available, Loaned, Reserved, Lost)
Repository interfaces for persistence
Specification pattern for composable search queries

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Two members checking out the last copy: atomic status transition on BookItem
Hold expires if not picked up: move to next in queue
Lost item: charge replacement cost, close loan
Returning an item not on loan or at a different branch
Member deleted with active loans: block or soft-delete

modelSummary: The model separates Book (catalog title) from BookItem (physical copy with barcode and status). Members borrow BookItems via Loans with due dates and return them through a LibraryService facade that enforces limits and fine thresholds. Holds are placed on a Book and queued FIFO; on return, the copy becomes RESERVED for the head of the queue and the member is notified via an Observer-driven NotificationService. Fines are computed by a pluggable FinePolicy. BookItem lifecycle uses the State pattern and status transitions are atomic to avoid double checkout. Classes: Library, LibraryService, Catalog, Book, BookItem, Account, Member, Librarian, Loan, Hold, Fine, FinePolicy, NotificationService.

title: Design a chess game with move validation
brief: Design the classes for a two-player chess game. The engine must validate moves according to the rules, detect check, checkmate and stalemate, and support castling, en passant and promotion. No AI opponent.
constraints: Standard 8x8 board, two human players
Full legal move validation including not leaving own king in check
Special moves: castling, en passant, promotion
Move history with undo
Detect checkmate, stalemate; optional draw rules

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
sections.prompt: Clarify rules and features in scope.
keyPoints: makeMove(from, to, promotion?) validates and applies or rejects
Turn order enforced; game states ACTIVE, CHECK, CHECKMATE, STALEMATE, RESIGNED
Undo last move; export PGN/FEN optional
Draw by threefold repetition and 50-move rule as stretch
Clock/timer out of scope

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: Game: board, players, current turn, status, move history
Board: 8x8 Square grid or Piece[64]; Position value object
Piece (abstract): color, type; subclasses King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Pawn
Move: from, to, piece, captured, special flag (castle, en passant, promotion)
Player; MoveValidator/RuleEngine

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
sections.prompt: How do pieces, board and rules interact?
keyPoints: Each Piece generates pseudo-legal moves: List<Move> candidateMoves(Board, Position)
Sliding pieces share a ray-walking helper (Rook/Bishop/Queen)
RuleEngine filters pseudo-legal moves by simulating and checking king safety
Game depends on RuleEngine; Board knows nothing of turns
Move objects are Commands with apply/undo on Board

sections.title: Key methods & flows
keyPoints: MoveResult Game.makeMove(Position from, Position to, PieceType promo)
Check piece exists and belongs to current player
legal = ruleEngine.legalMoves(board, from); match target else reject
move.apply(board); history.push(move); switch turn
status: inCheck(opponent) && no legal moves -> CHECKMATE; !inCheck && none -> STALEMATE
boolean isSquareAttacked(Board, Position, Color) used for check and castling path

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
keyPoints: Polymorphism/Strategy for per-piece movement
Command for Move with undo, enabling history and takeback
State for game status transitions
Factory to set up the initial board from FEN
Variants (Chess960) via a pluggable setup and castling rule

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Castling: king and rook unmoved, squares empty, king not in/through/into check
En passant only immediately after an opponent double pawn push (store en passant target)
Pinned pieces: handled by simulate-then-check-king approach
Promotion requires choice; default to queen if absent
Network play: server is authoritative; reject stale moves via move number

modelSummary: A Game holds a Board, two Players, turn, status and a stack of Move commands. Pieces are polymorphic and generate pseudo-legal moves; sliding pieces share a ray helper. A RuleEngine filters them by applying each move to the board, checking isSquareAttacked on the own king, and undoing, which naturally handles pins and check evasion. Special moves (castling, en passant, promotion) are flagged on Move and validated using board state such as castling rights and the en passant target. After each move the engine sets CHECK, CHECKMATE or STALEMATE. Move as Command enables undo and history. Classes: Game, Board, Position, Piece{King,Queen,Rook,Bishop,Knight,Pawn}, Move, MoveType, RuleEngine, Player, GameStatus.

title: Design a rate limiter library with strategies
brief: Design an in-process rate limiting library that application developers can drop into their services. It should support multiple algorithms, multiple limits per key, and be easy to extend with new algorithms or a distributed backing store later.
constraints: Algorithms: token bucket, fixed window, sliding window log/counter
Limits keyed by arbitrary string (user id, IP)
Thread-safe, low overhead (sub-microsecond for in-memory)
Pluggable clock for testing
Pluggable storage (in-memory now, Redis later)

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
keyPoints: boolean tryAcquire(key) and tryAcquire(key, permits)
Return decision with remaining and retryAfter for HTTP headers
Configure per rule: capacity/limit, window or refill rate
Multiple rules per key (all must pass)
Idle keys must not leak memory

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: RateLimiter interface: Decision tryAcquire(String key, int permits)
TokenBucketLimiter, FixedWindowLimiter, SlidingWindowLimiter implementations
RateLimitConfig (limit, window, refillRate)
Decision value object (allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs)
Clock interface; StateStore interface for bucket/window state

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
keyPoints: Strategy: algorithms implement RateLimiter
Limiters depend on StateStore and Clock abstractions (DIP)
CompositeRateLimiter combines several limiters (AND semantics)
RateLimiterFactory/Registry builds limiters from config
Middleware/filter integrates library with HTTP frameworks

sections.title: Key methods & flows
keyPoints: Decision TokenBucketLimiter.tryAcquire(key, n)
state = store.get(key) or new Bucket(capacity, now)
tokens = min(capacity, tokens + (now - last) * rate); last = now
if tokens >= n -> tokens -= n, allowed; else retryAfter = (n - tokens)/rate
Sliding window counter: estimate = prev * (1 - elapsed/window) + curr

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
keyPoints: New algorithm = new class implementing RateLimiter, registered in factory
Decorator to add metrics/logging to any limiter
Composite for multi-rule evaluation
Redis-backed store implements atomic ops via Lua script
Builder for fluent configuration

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Per-key atomicity: ConcurrentHashMap.compute or per-bucket lock/CAS
Avoid global locks; no lock held across stores
Composite: avoid consuming from rule A if rule B rejects (check-then-commit or refund)
Clock going backwards: clamp elapsed to >= 0
Evict idle keys via TTL or periodic sweep

modelSummary: The library exposes a RateLimiter interface returning a Decision (allowed, remaining, retryAfter). Algorithms are Strategy implementations: TokenBucketLimiter, FixedWindowLimiter, SlidingWindowLogLimiter and SlidingWindowCounterLimiter. Each depends on a Clock and a StateStore abstraction, so tests use a fake clock and production can swap in a Redis store with atomic Lua scripts. CompositeRateLimiter enforces several rules with check-then-commit semantics, and decorators add metrics. Per-key atomicity uses ConcurrentHashMap.compute or CAS, with idle keys expired. Classes: RateLimiter, Decision, RateLimitConfig, TokenBucketLimiter, FixedWindowLimiter, SlidingWindowLimiter, CompositeRateLimiter, StateStore, InMemoryStateStore, Clock, RateLimiterFactory.

title: Design a logger / event bus with sinks
brief: Design a logging framework (think a mini log4j/Serilog) where application code logs messages at levels, and messages are routed to multiple sinks such as console, file and a remote collector. Sinks can be added at runtime, and slow sinks must not block the application.
constraints: Levels: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL
Multiple sinks with independent level thresholds and formatters
Structured fields (key/value context) supported
Async delivery with bounded buffer
Hierarchical named loggers (com.app.db)

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
keyPoints: logger.info(msg, fields) and level-check shortcut isEnabled(level)
Per-logger and per-sink level filtering
Formatters: plain text, JSON
Ordering per logger preserved; at-most-once vs at-least-once to remote sink stated
Flush on shutdown

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: LoggerFactory/LogManager returns named Logger instances (cached)
Logger: name, level, list of sinks (or inherits from parent)
LogEvent: timestamp, level, loggerName, message, fields, thread, exception
Sink interface: write(LogEvent); ConsoleSink, FileSink, HttpSink
Formatter interface; Filter interface
AsyncDispatcher with bounded queue and worker thread

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
keyPoints: Logger -> Dispatcher -> many Sinks (publish/subscribe)
Each Sink has a Formatter and optional Filter (Strategy)
Logger hierarchy: child delegates to parent sinks unless additivity=false
Sinks implement Closeable for flush/shutdown
Same bus generalizes to an EventBus: topics -> subscribers

sections.title: Key methods & flows
sections.prompt: Walk a log call end to end.
keyPoints: void Logger.log(Level l, String msg, Map fields): if l < effectiveLevel return (cheap)
event = new LogEvent(clock.now(), l, name, msg, fields, MDC context)
dispatcher.enqueue(event) -> offer to bounded queue
Worker: for sink in sinks: if sink.accepts(event) sink.write(formatter.format(event))
void LogManager.shutdown(): drain queue, flush and close sinks

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
keyPoints: Observer/publish-subscribe between logger and sinks
Strategy for formatters, filters and overflow policy
Decorator: BufferedSink, RetryingSink, BatchingSink wrapping HttpSink
Singleton LogManager with factory for loggers
Chain of responsibility for filters

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Bounded queue overflow policy: block, drop newest, drop DEBUG first; count drops
One slow sink must not stall others: per-sink queue/worker
Sink exception is caught and reported to an internal error handler, never thrown to app
Lazy message formatting (supplier) to avoid cost when level disabled
File rotation by size/time with atomic rename

modelSummary: A LogManager hands out cached, hierarchically named Logger instances that do a cheap level check then build an immutable LogEvent with timestamp, level, message, structured fields and context. Events are enqueued on a bounded AsyncDispatcher queue; worker threads fan them out to registered Sinks (Observer/pub-sub). Each Sink has its own level threshold, Filter and Formatter (Strategy), and decorators add batching, buffering and retry. Overflow policy is explicit and drop counts are reported; sink exceptions are isolated. Shutdown drains and flushes. Classes: LogManager, Logger, Level, LogEvent, Dispatcher, AsyncDispatcher, Sink{ConsoleSink,FileSink,HttpSink}, Formatter{TextFormatter,JsonFormatter}, Filter, BatchingSink.

title: Design a vending machine
brief: Design the software for a vending machine. Users insert coins or bills, select a product, receive the product and change, or cancel and get a refund. Model it with clean state transitions.
constraints: Products in slots with price and quantity
Accepts coins and bills of fixed denominations
Must return exact change or refuse the sale
Admin can restock items and collect cash
Single user at a time

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
keyPoints: Insert money, select product, dispense, return change, cancel/refund
Reject selection if sold out or insufficient funds
Refuse sale if exact change cannot be made
Admin restock and cash collection mode
Display messages for each state

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: VendingMachine context: current state, inventory, balance, cash box
State interface with IdleState, HasMoneyState, DispensingState, MaintenanceState
Inventory: Map<SlotCode, Slot(product, qty)>
Product (name, price); Coin/Bill denominations enum
CashBox/ChangeMaker holding denomination counts

sections.title: Relationships & interfaces
keyPoints: VendingMachine delegates every action to its current State
States receive the machine as context to transition: machine.setState(...)
ChangeMaker strategy computes change from available denominations
Dispenser and Display hardware behind interfaces for testing
Inventory and CashBox are owned by the machine

sections.title: Key methods & flows
keyPoints: void insertMoney(Denomination d) -> state.insertMoney(this, d)
void selectProduct(SlotCode c): check qty>0, balance>=price, change computable
Map<Denomination,Integer> ChangeMaker.makeChange(amount, available) (greedy for canonical sets, DP otherwise)
dispense: inventory.decrement, cashBox.commit, return change, setState(Idle)
List<Denomination> cancel(): refund inserted money, go Idle

sections.title: Patterns & extensibility
keyPoints: State pattern removes large switch statements per action
Strategy for change making and payment methods (card later)
Observer for low-stock alerts to operator
Command for admin operations
Adding card payment = new PaymentMethod and maybe a new state

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Dispense jam: refund or retry; do not decrement inventory until confirmed
Power loss mid-transaction: persist balance before acting
Invalid/counterfeit currency rejected at insert
Inserting money in Dispensing state is rejected and returned
Greedy change fails for non-canonical sets; use DP with limited counts

modelSummary: VendingMachine is the context of a State pattern with IdleState, HasMoneyState, DispensingState and MaintenanceState; each public action (insertMoney, selectProduct, cancel, restock) delegates to the current state, which validates and transitions. Inventory maps slot codes to products and quantities, and a CashBox tracks denomination counts. A ChangeMaker strategy computes exact change with limited coin counts (DP when greedy is unsafe) and the sale is refused if change is impossible. Inventory is decremented only after the dispenser confirms. Hardware sits behind Dispenser and Display interfaces. Classes: VendingMachine, State{Idle,HasMoney,Dispensing,Maintenance}, Inventory, Slot, Product, Denomination, CashBox, ChangeMaker, Dispenser, Display.

title: Design a meeting room scheduler
brief: Design a meeting room booking system for a company (think Outlook room booking). Users search for available rooms by time, capacity and equipment, book them, and may create recurring meetings. Double booking must never happen.
constraints: Multiple buildings with rooms having capacity and equipment
Bookings in 15-minute granularity, time zones matter
Recurring meetings (daily/weekly) with exceptions
Concurrent booking attempts for the same room
Notify attendees on create/update/cancel

sections.title: Requirements & use cases
keyPoints: Search available rooms for [start,end) with capacity and features
Book, update, cancel; recurring series with single-instance edits
No overlapping bookings per room (half-open intervals)
Attendee invites and notifications
Non-goals: full calendar sync with external providers

sections.title: Core classes & responsibilities
keyPoints: Room (id, building, floor, capacity, features)
Meeting/Booking (id, room, organizer, attendees, interval, status)
TimeSlot/Interval value object with overlaps()
RecurrenceRule (frequency, interval, until/count, exceptions)
Scheduler/BookingService; RoomRepository; Calendar per room

keyPoints: Room 1..* Bookings via a RoomCalendar (sorted interval structure)
RecurringSeries generates Booking instances; exceptions override instances
RoomSearch uses Specification/filters for capacity and features
NotificationService (Observer) on booking events
RoomSelectionStrategy for suggesting best room (smallest fit, nearest)

keyPoints: List<Room> findAvailable(Interval i, int capacity, Set<Feature> f)
Booking book(roomId, Interval i, User org, List<User> attendees)

Series bookRecurring(roomId, Interval first, RecurrenceRule r): expand instances, all-or-nothing or report conflicts
void cancel(bookingId) -> remove from calendar, notify

keyPoints: Strategy for room selection; Specification for filters
Observer for notifications
Interval tree or sorted map per room for overlap queries

Extend to desks or equipment by generalizing Room to Resource

sections.title: Concurrency & edge cases
keyPoints: Check-and-insert on RoomCalendar must be atomic: per-room lock
In a DB: exclusion constraint on (room, tsrange) or SELECT FOR UPDATE
Recurring booking conflicts: report which instances fail
Store UTC, render in local time; DST shifts for recurring meetings
Back-to-back meetings allowed with half-open [start,end)

modelSummary: Rooms carry capacity and features; each Room has a RoomCalendar storing bookings in a sorted map keyed by start time so isFree(interval) is an O(log n) neighbour check on half-open intervals. BookingService handles search (filtered by Specification and ranked by a RoomSelectionStrategy), book, update and cancel. Recurring meetings are a RecurringSeries with a RecurrenceRule that expands to instances, with per-instance exceptions. Double booking is prevented with a per-room lock in memory or a database exclusion constraint. Times are stored in UTC and recurrence is expanded in the organizer time zone. Notifications use Observer. Classes: Room, Building, Feature, Interval, Booking, RecurringSeries, RecurrenceRule, RoomCalendar, BookingService, RoomSelectionStrategy, NotificationService.
